title.narrative: USAID Support for Indonesia Climate Change Trust Fund (ICCTF)

description.narrative: (Indonesia): The Indonesian Climate Change Trust Fund (ICCTF) was established in 2009 by the GOI to boost investment in Indonesia's climate resilience and low carbon economy by consolidating and increasing access to private, public, and international climate finance. ICCTF serves as a mechanism for multilateral and bilateral development partners to make financial pledges to pool resources to support climate change mitigation and adaptation activities aligned with the GOI's National Climate Mitigation Action Plan (RAN-GRK) and National Climate Adaptation Plan (RAN-API).~USAID supports the plan of the Government of Indonesia to cut the country's carbon emissions by 26 percent by 2020 through protection of forests and peat lands with international aid.~ USAID/Indonesia's $5 million contribution to ICCTF will fund a suite of projects with Indonesian local organizations to 1) reduce Indonesian greenhouse gas emissions from the land use sector, and 2) facilitate adaptation to climate change Indonesia.~The~ICCTF~is one of only two nationally managed trust funds in the world dedicated to fighting climate change, and is a model for many middle-income and developing countries.

title.narrative: UK FCDO Green Economic Growth Support

description.narrative: The programme aims to promote green growth in Papua. It will contribute to the government of Papuas vision and spatial plan that intends to preserve 90 per cent forest cover in the province. In doing so the programme will support the provinces transition away from a high carbon business as usual growth trajectory onto a low carbon development pathway. The programme is designed to address the key barriers to private sector development in Papua that will enable firms to pursue low carbon business opportunities. It will work directly with firms, the financial sector, and the public sector to improve the commercial and environmental sustainability of small and medium sized enterprises. In addition, the programme will generate knowledge on how green growth can be implemented in Indonesia and globally.

title.narrative: Kartu Prakerja: Evaluating Indonesias Job Training and Cash Transfer Program

description.narrative: Nearly two-thirds of Indonesias 270.2 million people struggle to meet their immediate needs for food and other basics, largely due to underemployment and skills gaps that prevent workers from entering the formal economy. To address employment challenges, the Government of Indonesia launched a social assistance program in 2020 that provides temporarily unemployed peoplesuch as those who were laid off or small business owners who were impacted by the COVID-19 pandemicwith money and online vocational training. This program, known as Kartu Prakerja (KP) (Indonesian for pre-employment card), builds on a large body of research on vocational training and cash transfers that aim to help individuals find gainful employment, meet their needs, and invest in their families futures. Since the inception of the program, nearly 29 million individuals have applied to KP and 5.9 million have been randomly selected to participate in it. Because this program is new, little is known about its effects. To explore the potential impact of the program, an international team of economists and researchers coordinated by Harvard University is conducting an at-scale impact evaluation of the program in partnership with the Government of Indonesia. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, the team will improve the rigor of the study by expanding it to include a second round of surveys of the control group of 10,000 people who do not receive KP benefits. Researchers will also run two randomized controlled trials to test the relative effects of several features of KP. This research will generate critical evidence on this massive social protection program and inform policymakers in other countries seeking to ease pandemic-related and other relatively short-term economic hardships through effective social assistance programs.

title.narrative: Nolkup: An App to Access Low Arsenic Water in Bangladesh.

description.narrative: Toxic levels of arsenic contaminate one-third of tubewells in rural Bangladesh and affect the drinking water of up to 100 million people. An estimated 100,000 annual deaths in Bangladesh have been linked to chronic arsenic exposure from drinking well-water. To help families know which wells are contaminated, Columbia University developed the Nolkup (tubewell in Bangla) smartphone app. A tubewell is a common type of water well in Bangladesh. The location-based app tells the user the arsenic content of tested wells nearby so they can make informed decisions about where to obtain water. Traditionally, environmental information is communicated via costly and lengthy door-to-door information campaigns, if at all. Nolkup is a convenient and cost-effective method of delivering public information on arsenic levels. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, Columbia University is running a randomized controlled trial to test whether the technology can have positive effects on behaviors and decision-making but more quickly and at lower cost. The Bangladesh governments Department of Public Health Engineering is responsible for testing wells under its Arsenic Risk Reduction Program and has agreed to make five to ten million well test results available on Nolkup. Columbia University is testing the app in partnership with the NGO Forum and Innovations for Poverty Action Bangladesh. By testing the effectiveness of app-based water quality information services, Columbia University and its partners will measure if this low-cost solution leads to higher utilization of clean drinking water. That in turn will inform effective ways to leverage the data being collected by the government on five to ten million wells.

description.narrative: (Indonesia): The Developmental Evaluation (DE) Jalin has demonstrated its ability to improve the effectiveness of the implementation of the USAID Jalin project through continuous learning and adaptation. In addition to enabling adaptive management of the USAID Jalin activity, the DE also provided assistance to the Ministry of Health (MOH) to develop maps of health facilities' maternal and newborn services to use in national-level discussions on the management of the healthcare system and development of new maternal-newborn health initiatives. USAID will continue using DE to provide adaptive management support to USAID Jalin in third year of implementation. .Based on the first year of implementation, the MOH recognized the value of using DE's methodology to provide real-time feedback and to improve program implementation. MOH has requested USAID to support implementing a developmental evaluation methodology for monitoring and evaluation of a new MOH national initiative on Maternal and Newborn Health. The new initiative includes a Special Allocation Fund (SAF) for MCH and a National Mentoring Program. DE will support the MOH in establishing a developmental evaluation system and conduct capacity building for MOH staff to implement and conduct DE methodology..

title.narrative: USAID Mobilizing Networks for Self-reliance to Fight TB (Mandiri-TB)

description.narrative: (Indonesia): The TB Local Organizations Network is a key component of the USAID Global Accelerator to End Tuberculosis. The TB LON also leverages additional resources from countries, private sector partners, and other local organizations to meet the UN Target of treating 40 million people by 2022 through provision of accessible services, resulting in increased diagnosis and treatment success rates..USAID-funded Mandiri-TB (Mobilizing Networks for Self-Reliance to Fight TB/Mobilisasi Jejaring untuk Kemandirian Melawan TB) project builds Indonesia self-reliance in ending TB. This is achieved by empowering the networks of local TB stakeholders such as the district government, health providers, civil society organizations as well private-owned institutions. Mobilizing and empowering networks of TB stakeholders displays commitment and ability to plan, finance and implement solutions to solve local challenges in eliminating TB. ..To achieve this, Mandiri-TB focuses on two strategies: .Multi-sectoral approach to motivate the government and corporate sector to increase funding for TB elimination. .Empower TB civil societies and patient organizations to strengthen peer support and case management of DR-TB patients. ..The activity will contribute to the Indo-Pacific Strategy and the U.S. Mission objective of supporting Indonesia's greater global and regional role promoting democratic values, rule of law, and protecting the environment, public health, and other shared priorities.

title.narrative: USAID Indonesia Indonesia Coffee Enterprise Resilience Initiative (Resilient Coffee)

description.narrative: This award will increase access to finance, climate resilience, and gender equality and social inclusion for small and medium sized coffee enterprises (SMEs) in Indonesia. USAID will leverage its local expertise to help build smallholder resilience by expanding access to finance for farmers and small coffee enterprises that lack access to credit and business education. The program will work with businesses to strengthen gender equity and social inclusion practices while implementing new digital solutions to improve the management and resilience of coffee enterprises. Finally, the partners will strengthen climate action in the coffee industry, with a focus on mitigating climate change, protecting vulnerable ecosystems, and supporting rural communities to adapt to climate impacts.

title.narrative: Financial Inclusion of Women-Led Small and Medium Enterprises (FINCLUSION for W-SMEs)

description.narrative: Financial Inclusion of Women-Led Small and Medium Enterprises (FINCLUSION for W-SMEs) will improve access to financing for W-SMEs throughout Indonesia. The partnership will provide networking opportunities, share information on accessible financial products, and improve W-SMEs financial management knowledge and digital literacy. The partnership has developed a public platform for financial and digital training, as well as a private platform to target selected women SME owners nominated by their banks for additional training, leading to a loan offer. This new partnership will accelerate inclusive economic growth, while expanding public-private capacity and investing in womens economic empowerment.

description.narrative: (Indonesia): .LESTARI is a partnership between the GOI and USAID that aims to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and conserve biodiversity in carbon rich and biologically significant forest and mangrove ecosystems. At least 30 million people depend directly on Indonesia's forests for their livelihoods. Indonesia's deforestation rates ranking among the highest in the world and their biodiversity continues to be under serious threat. A history of weak governance combined with opportunistic private sector actors has created unsustainable natural resource exploitation. LESTARI addresses these issues in six strategic landscapes in the provinces of Aceh, Central Kalimantan, and Papua. It applies a landscape-based approach to conserve biodiversity and reduce GHG emissions, integrating forest and peatland conservation with low emissions development. It is achieved through strengthening land use governance, enhanced protected areas management and protection of key species (elephant, tiger, orangutan), sustainable private sector and industry practices, and expanded constituencies for conservation among various stakeholders. Specifically, orangutan conservation will continue to ensure the $2.5 million earmark goes towards practical and sustainable solutions. USAID continues rehabilitation and release of captive orangutans into a national park. LESTARI with and through stakeholders is a catalyst for self-sufficient, transparent, and sustainable solutions to natural resource governance challenges. LESTARI contributes to the U.S. Mission objective of supporting Indonesia's greater global and regional role promoting democratic values, rule of law, and protecting the environment, public health, and other shared priorities. Effective natural resource management, including the protection of its biodiversity, by the government of Indonesia also positively contributes to its long-term economic prosperity and is a core component of Indonesia's journey to self-reliance..

The consequences of poor water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services are felt most acutely by low-income families in urban areas. Through the Water for the World Act, the U.S. Government is helping improve WASH conditions in Indonesia, a priority country for USAID. Indonesia is committed to achieving 100 percent universal access to safe water and proper sanitation in alignment with the 2030 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals for both water and sanitation. Through the 5.5-year (2016-2021), $48,357,584 million USAID IUWASH PLUS project (including a $4.5 million contribution from the Government of Switzerland), USAID is building Indonesia's capacity to reduce barriers to safely-managed water and sanitation services. .USAID IUWASH PLUS works with governmental and donor agencies, the private sector, NGOs, service utilities and communities to strengthen the overall WASH 'ecosystem' in urban Indonesia. USAID through IUWASH PLUS strengthens the capacity of the providers of water and sanitation services to ensure that improved access is maintained over the long term. These partnerships are lowering the costs of WASH services for the most vulnerable Indonesians, contributing to life-saving gains in access and reducing the threat of waterborne diseases. description.narrative: IBTCI has been contracted to conduct an evaluation of the joint USAID/USG Volcano Disaster Assistance Program (VDAP) and its contribution to hazard monitoring in Indonesia since 2004.
